headline: Ombudsman Files Plunder Case Against Martin Romualdez Over Alleged Flood-Control Kickback Scheme
seoTitle: Ombudsman Files Plunder Case Against Martin Romualdez | FMB News
seoDescription: The Ombudsman filed a plunder case against Martin Romualdez and three others over an alleged ₱7.4-billion flood-control kickback scheme. The allegations remain unproven.
deck: The Ombudsman filed a plunder case against Martin Romualdez and three others over an alleged ₱7.4-billion flood-control kickback scheme. Romualdez has denied wrongdoing, and the accusations remain unproven.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Office of the Ombudsman filed a plunder case at the Sandiganbayan on September 7 against former House Speaker and incumbent Leyte 1st District Representative Martin Romualdez and three other respondents over an alleged kickback scheme involving flood-control projects.

GMA News reported that Assistant Ombudsman Mico Clavano confirmed the anti-graft court had received the case. Reporting based on the court filing identifies the other respondents as former Ako Bicol representative Zaldy Co, Joselyn Tragua Serenio and Felicito Cristobal Guevarra.

The case alleges a ₱7.4-billion scheme. That amount and the alleged kickbacks are accusations contained in the prosecution case; they have not been proven in court. Romualdez has repeatedly denied involvement in illegal flood-control transactions and has challenged the credibility of evidence previously raised against him.

DZRH reported after the court raffle that the case was assigned to the Sandiganbayan Third Division. The division will determine the next judicial steps, including whether probable cause exists for the issuance of warrants.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The filing moves the controversy from an Ombudsman investigation into a criminal case before the anti-graft court. Earlier Ombudsman proceedings examined allegations involving public funds and infrastructure projects, while Romualdez’s legal team submitted counter-affidavits and witness statements disputing the accusations.

Some witnesses whose earlier statements were cited in the wider flood-control investigation later recanted. Romualdez’s lawyers have argued that the recantations and other defense evidence undermine the allegations against him. The filing of a case does not establish guilt, and the court has not yet adjudicated the merits of the accusations.

Malacañang acknowledged the Ombudsman filing on September 7. Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said the administration respects the Ombudsman process and reiterated President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s position that accountability should apply regardless of personal or political relationships.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: Flood-control spending affects public safety, disaster resilience and the use of billions of pesos in taxpayer funds. A criminal case involving a former House Speaker and allegations tied to infrastructure appropriations therefore has consequences beyond the individual defendants: it tests whether institutions can examine alleged misuse of public funds through a transparent judicial process.

For readers, the key distinction is between a verified procedural fact and an unproven criminal allegation. It is confirmed that the Ombudsman filed the case and that the Sandiganbayan received it. Whether the accused committed plunder is a question for the court and must not be treated as established fact unless and until proven through the judicial process.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The next material developments are the Sandiganbayan Third Division’s review of probable cause, any warrants or court orders it may issue, and the formal responses of Romualdez and the other respondents to the filed charge.

FMB News will also watch for the official case docket, subsequent pleadings and court resolutions that clarify the precise prosecution theory and evidence. New claims from either side will be treated as claims unless independently established by official records or credible corroboration.

verificationNotes: The central event is verified: GMA News reported from the Sandiganbayan that Assistant Ombudsman Mico Clavano confirmed the court received the filing; PNA separately reported Malacañang’s acknowledgment of the Ombudsman case.
DZRH separately reported that the case was raffled to the Sandiganbayan Third Division after filing.
The ₱7.4-billion figure is presented as the amount alleged in the filed plunder case, not as proven loss or proven ill-gotten wealth.
Romualdez’s denials and defense position are included to preserve the distinction between charges and established facts. Filing a criminal case does not establish guilt.
